Resolved by P15 part 4 (OPUS-PEOPLE, 2026-10-10): the look-up act answers a cause's need to know where to go, is offered only to people with a cause, and offers only the offices (with staff), meeting places and groups of a kind they know none of (office-directory in src/core2/modules/people.ts); company comes from people.
replacement: Knowledge-qualified directory offers and utility tied to actual information needs, with end-to-end ordinary cause/action evidence.

whatItFakes: Stress-derived safety utility favors organizing immediately after acute bereavement without a grief response favoring withdrawal and family.
why: P10 reports a widow organized on the day her husband died; CTO REVIEW 11 requires grief to first pull toward withdrawal and family. Resolved by P15 part 4 (OPUS-PEOPLE, 2026-10-10): a death gives each relative grief that pulls toward rest and contact with family and holds back organizing, fading by their own resilience line (src/core2/grief.ts); registered as SG-P15-grief-line.
replacement: A source-qualified evolving bereavement state and choice contributions that preserve variation, family context and actual later cause formation.

whatItFakes: Historical acquaintances are seeded for the player alone and carry no dated shared moments keyed to both people. Other residents have no generated acquaintance history for a reunion to read.
why: CTO REVIEW 12 reports P13 proof #3929: La Homa has only the player’s twenty faded school acquaintances and no recorded shared moment. This is a P13 finding, not independently rerun here. Resolved Oct 16, 2026 (core-standins-opening-deletions): by the two-level rule only the player's circle and people they meet carry history, and a person filled in later is seeded from the world; the shared-past generator for everyone is not built.
replacement: Generate source-qualified classmates, coworkers, neighbors and congregation acquaintances for everyone, with dated pair-keyed shared moments and realistic network spreads. Preserve genuine supplied shared history.

whatItFakes: Unconditional CEX service means become capped fictional household opening budgets with named counterparties. National component proportions scale regional/household-size parent categories. Equal initial vendor shares are recorded terms, not measured choice.
why: Source means do not establish individual needs, supplier scope, recurring bill dates, delivered services or a per-world person dispersion.
replacement: Use recorded individual budgets and product-compatible agreements plus matched service-level size/region priors and actor purchasing producers.

whatItFakes: Retrospective aggregate public-building spending, estimated cleaning/coverage fractions and saved fictional authority/appropriation produce bounded custodial budgets. The modeled source is not a real 2021 county or CDP appropriation.
why: County identity and geographic reach do not observe enacted appropriation, price, award or treasury authority. Zero-stock due-flow accounting cannot manufacture that legal/source crosswalk.
replacement: The later public-budget, procurement and intergovernmental-transfers modules provide dated own-government authority, appropriation, award/agreement, price, supplier scope and actual source-owned payment calendar. Preserve actual county owner IDs and never invent a La Homa CDP municipal budget.

whatItFakes: One synthetic family/visit identity and CEX lodging budget still preload a $7,400 SCF2022 transaction-account prior. REVIEW15/16 require outside obligations to be incoming due flows instead of an imported stock.
why: Actual geography and national household wealth/expenditure means do not establish this buyer balance, real trip, invoice cadence, vendor choice or outside-demand share at a 2021 opening. Resolved Oct 16, 2026 (core-standins-opening-deletions): the made-up visiting family is deleted. A town's firms already sell to buyers outside it through the outside market (each firm's receipts times its industry's sourced outside share, paid from one outside account), so a motel's guests are carried there; the synthetic family layered a second source on top.
replacement: The later national-external-economy, regional travel and outside-customer modules provide genuine dated visit/order/price/payment terms and product-qualified buyers/sellers. Keep outside opening cash zero and signed net flow separate; source additional territory geography without invented series.

whatItFakes: A proposed source-owned public-payroll bridge would use saved estimated hourly work/pay terms and an explicitly linked modeled paying authority to fund only each genuine current attended-work obligation; it would not claim actual historical salary entitlement or appropriation.
why: The current public owner/job/pay/schedule records do not reconstruct 2021 employment authority, appropriation, deductions, pension contributions or government treasury funding.
replacement: The later public-budget/public-payroll module owns actual legal employment/pay authority, salary calendars, deductions and employer-to-treasury links; national/federal-state transfers supply dated external obligations. No bare external flag or projected payroll grants payment authority.

whatItFakes: The current twelve zero-receipt booked firms have no product-qualified customer classification route. A proposed extension still needs actual product/service, buyer need/order and dated amount/price records; no uniform outside-demand percentage is measured.
why: Industry payroll/IRS ratios and aggregate CFS international shipments do not identify town-firm product scope, actual outside buyer agreement or a 2021 macro demand path.
replacement: The later national-external-economy/trade and industry-specific customer modules provide matched commodity/service geography, buyer/order/delivery scope and dated demand/price priors. Freight, construction, insurance, realty, care and tuition retain distinct obligations and authorities.

whatItFakes: First-next-period-month payment and a twelve-month source-year budget horizon are generated conventions; the annual statistical source does not observe any actual contract expiry or renewal.
why: CEX annual expenditure and aggregate public fiscal-year data cannot choose an individual invoice day or legally end a standing due obligation.
replacement: The later public-budget/procurement and national-external-customer modules supply actual dated agreements, invoice/calendar and amendment/renewal/end records. Preserve supplied real ends; do not fabricate a one-year legal cutoff.

whatItFakes: Generated private-employer opening cash stock from real JPMC quartile/median anchors and an explicitly estimated WHO prior times scheduled payroll plus a compatible IRS nonwage accounting-cost proxy; not observed individual cash or an owner equity transaction.
why: The observed bank-account/all-debit sample differs from a generated local/territorial employer and accounting-cost proxy. Firm legal form, total size, cash-debit coverage, banking coverage, actual owner capital and individual crosswalk remain unmeasured; observed quartiles do not establish them.
replacement: Recorded firm opening balances and capital provenance, or a matched ALL-debit/balance cohort adapter with honest distributions and measured crosswalk evidence. No survival-based stock tuning or fictional contribution.

whatItFakes: A WHO-only stable per-firm startup cash-buffer rank and continuous quantile curve with one authored tail-span coefficient. Published q25/median/q75 are real observations; the full CDF and endpoints are estimates.
why: Observed cohort quartiles do not identify individual firm liquidity, uniform identity ranks, piecewise-linear interpolation, tail extrema or a coefficient uncertainty interval. Generated legal form, location, vintage and ALL-cash-debit denominator differ from the selected employer/nonemployer Chase sample.
replacement: Recorded individual firm liquidity/capital provenance or an independently observed matched ALL-cash-debit/balance cohort distribution with identified crosswalk and tail evidence. Never calibrate to future closures or wages surviving a requested year.

whatItFakes: Fresh generated public, institution, nonbusiness and unknown owners open with modeled zero-funded prototype journal cash pending genuine dated funding. The technical zero is not an observed zero balance and has no private-business calibration.
why: The superseded six-month payroll stock has no observed institutional balance, dated appropriation or funding receipt. Private JPMC employer/nonemployer cash evidence cannot supply those missing public or other unsupported owner facts.
replacement: REVIEW16 public-budget and national modules must supply genuine dated funding authority, appropriations and treasury/account receipts for represented institutions; other unsupported owners need separately source-qualified recorded funding. Preserve actual supplied balances. Never infer a measured zero, private JPMC reserve, survival stock or synthetic owner contribution.

whatItFakes: Carries a genuinely observed active 2017 county identity forward to the opening date using its official stable GID/PID alias and an already existing canonical county account. Intermediate identity-change history and actual opening active status remain unobserved.
why: The 2017 Census government listing was recorded before the January 1, 2021 opening; a later canonical directory cannot be backdated. Historical identity supplies an owner candidate, not legal powers, enacted appropriation or opening cash.
replacement: A dated opening government directory or independently sourced legal identity/change history matched to the same official government ID. Preserve the original 2017 observation date and account ID.

whatItFakes: Uses existing generated person countyIds and the observed 2020 county-to-place relation to qualify the represented share of a bounded opening purchase plan. Recorded geography and residency do not observe public demand, appropriation, custodial supplier reach, travel or delivery.
why: The county keeps its county jurisdiction while the represented cohort lives in a CDP. Census geography was observed April 1, 2020 but published August 12, 2021, so an earlier opening uses it only as a retrospective generation prior. Unverified membership remains unbound.
replacement: Dated own-county procurement/service-area records and actual contract scope with matched represented-resident coverage. A verified geographic relation alone must not close the existing public-procurement appropriation/price stopgap.

whatItFakes: Fresh employer-owned payroll frequency/phase/lag calendars estimated from dated business-frequency evidence and separately qualified public/education examples; no actual fictional employer term or legal compliance claimed.
why: Current owned work has attendance timetables and hourly wage proxies but no historical paycheck calendar. BLS business shares do not identify employer phase/lag, current headcount, government/education weights or payroll-group membership. Farm/unknown extrapolation, no-adjustment holidays and model boundaries remain unmeasured.
replacement: Qualified employer-owned dated compensation/payroll records and government/education policy calendars, actual legal-frequency/holiday/lag treatment, shared household payday source links and empirical startup cohort checks. Public-budget/national modules own actual government funding, not this timing prior.

whatItFakes: On a minimum wage's effective date the laws module replaces each underpaid work commitment's hourly rate directly in core work state.
why: core2 has no pay-change path: admitWorkCommitment is the only writer and no API ends or re-rates a commitment.
replacement: OPUS-CORE's work pay-change API (re-rate a commitment from a date with its source), called here instead.
resolution: Replaced by OPUS-CORE's rerateJob (core2-api-v12) in laws.ts raiseOne and raiseToFloor; counted residents' jobs rise too.

whatItFakes: A state or federal officeholder outside the town is a stable identity (name, gender, birth date, party) with no core2 person behind it.
why: core2 has no fill-in yet: a named person outside the town can't become a full person when clicked. Resolved by OPUS-OFFICIALS (2026-10-13): every state and federal official outside the town is filled in at the opening as a full person with traits, views, a party wing, a career and colleagues (src/core2/modules/officials.ts); a holder seated later is filled in the first time their seat is read.
replacement: CORE's two-level fill-in builds the full person from this identity (seeded from the world and the seat), with kin and a past from PEOPLE.

whatItFakes: A law whose first recorded phase begins after the January 20, 2025 start (most income tax, sales tax, property tax, SNAP, unemployment and Medicaid rows begin October 2025 or January 2026) is in force from the start at that phase's terms, labeled as an estimate.
why: The starting-law research was compiled for a 2026 start; the owner moved the start to January 20, 2025 on October 14, 2026, and a law in force must never be unknown.
replacement: Sourced phases in force on January 20, 2025 for each series and place in src/core2/data/laws/starting-law.json (2025 tax brackets and rates, FY2025 SNAP maximums and Medicaid match, 2025 unemployment maximums).

whatItFakes: The end of each term in progress at the opening for state and local offices: the seats of a body take turns over the years in one term that the office's calendar (the county schedule or the state's municipal election law) holds elections, and each term ends on the start day after its seat's election; where a state's own start rule isn't read, January 1 (the governors' clauses of AK, CA, CO, DE, FL, HI, IL, LA, ME, NJ, OH, OK, PA, VA and WA are read, and, as estimates from the usual clause or the current governor's date, AZ, CT, GA, ID, IN, KS, MD, MN, MT, NE, NV, OR, TX, UT, VT, WI and WY are set, in data/elections/term-starts.json). Federal terms are read: every House seat ends January 3 of an odd year (amend. XX), Senate seats by their real class, the presidency on January 20.
why: Real election calendars and term-start dates for each office are M2's filing and election work.
replacement: The other states' governor start clauses and the state-legislature start days read into data/elections/term-starts.json, and municipal timing from the 92O baselines (county bodies are read: county-election-schedule-by-state.json).

whatItFakes: A special election for a seat no race engine counts (a statewide executive seat, a judge, a seat of another body) goes to the best-suited eligible person on the day instead of a vote. The town's own seats are real races in the voting engine, and a House or legislative district outside the town is counted by the world races (named party candidates, the winner serves the unexpired term). The date is the state's law for the office where special-election-law.json reads it, else the 90-day estimate (SG-GOV-special-election-timing).
why: The world races count only House and legislative districts; the other kinds have no counted race yet. Narrowed Oct 19 (claude/special-election-races).
replacement: Each office's special-election timing from its law (many fill at the next general election).

whatItFakes: Every adult resident counts as a registered voter where filing or signing requires registration.
why: core2 has no voter registration record yet. Retired by Session C, October 15, 2026: the eligibility check inferred registration solely from age and residence. The owner's no-paperwork rule does not call for a registration mechanic. Filing no longer reports that invented status; sourced research metadata is retained.
replacement: Retired the unsupported registered-voter eligibility result. Age, residence, deadlines, party membership and term limits remain separate checks. Reintroduce a registration mechanic only if the owner or golden path calls for it, with actual records.

whatItFakes: Each person's stance on a policy question is their lean times the question's measured left-right axis. Where PEOPLE's views engine runs, the lean orders people by their own view (CES 2024 cell plus household); elsewhere, by three personality facets. The order is then placed against the area's real 2024 vote.
why: OPUS-PEOPLE's views engine (values and stances formed from each person's life) isn't on core2 yet.
replacement: Per-question stances from PEOPLE's views engine, once it holds stances by question at the opening.

whatItFakes: An ad reaches the adults with the fewest work hours, as a stand-in for who watches and scrolls most; ad time is bought from a stand-in local media seller.
why: People's media habits and the news outlets aren't modeled on core2 yet. Resolved Oct 16: ad time is bought from the press's town outlet and reaches that outlet's followers; with no press there is no outlet, so nothing is bought. The stand-in seller and the fewest-work-hours viewers are deleted.
replacement: Each person's media habits and real outlets (PEOPLE and the news engine); ads bought from those outlets.

whatItFakes: Where the town records no professional-services business (NAICS 5419 includes public opinion polling), a campaign's poll interviews are paid to a stand-in pollster organization in town.
why: Small towns often have no polling firm; the region's businesses outside the town aren't recorded as sellers a campaign can reach.
replacement: The region's or state's real polling firms (County Business Patterns NAICS 541910 by county) as recorded organizations a campaign buys from.

whatItFakes: Where the town records no professional-services or manufacturing business (direct mail advertising, NAICS 54186; printing, NAICS 323), a campaign's mailers are paid to a stand-in mail house in town, postage included.
why: The region's printers and mail houses outside the town aren't recorded as sellers, and postage isn't paid to a postal organization.
replacement: The region's printers and mail houses (County Business Patterns) as recorded sellers, with postage paid to the Postal Service's account.

whatItFakes: Where the town records no recreation, lodging or food-service business, a campaign event's venue rent is paid to a stand-in venue in town.
why: Public halls (a town's own community center, a school gym) aren't recorded as places a campaign rents.
replacement: The town's public buildings and halls as rentable places with their fee schedules, and the region's venues.

whatItFakes: In a nonpartisan or local race, voters the world doesn't name vote as lean bands around the place's lean, sized from the town's population times the 2024 share of people who voted, each band voting with its named people. (Partisan state and federal races now count them in blocks: src/core2/electorate-blocks.ts.) The figures are researched: 0.46 of residents vote on a presidential date, scaled by cycle (midterm 0.72, off-cycle 0.39; Hajnal and Green 2024); what stays a stand-in is the local groups themselves.
why: CORE's voter groups exist as a table but generated worlds don't populate them yet. Resolved by the one-electorate change (owner, Oct 14, 2026): the lean bands and the group store are deleted; the rest of a local race's electorate (the town's population past its counted residents) votes on the counted residents' own engine (src/core2/electorate.ts countPlaces), and no race sizes its electorate from a share of population any more.
replacement: CORE's populated voter groups (counts by place, age, job and household, with lean and turnout), each voting as a group.

whatItFakes: When filing closes, the incumbent stands again if alive, and each state or federal race gets a named challenger from the other major party.
why: OPUS-PEOPLE's 'who runs' (M2-04) isn't built: people deciding to run from their drives, views and circumstances.
replacement: PEOPLE's who-runs decisions file each candidate through fileCandidacy with recorded reasons; incumbents decide the same way.

whatItFakes: Counties and cities start their fiscal year on their state's date.
why: City and county fiscal calendars aren't researched yet (M1-budgets-taxes research item 1).
replacement: Each county's and city's own fiscal year start and adoption deadline, from charters and budget documents, with estimates for the rest.
resolvedBy: OPUS-GOV, Oct 12: each county and city takes its state's same-type Census 2024 sampled unit nearest in population (src/core2/data/budgets/local-fiscal-years.json), else the national most common year end.

whatItFakes: Local spending is shared between county and city by function (counties: welfare, health and hospitals, corrections, highways, natural resources; cities and townships: the rest), and local revenue in the same proportion.
why: Census reports local government finances combined, not by government. Resolved by OPUS-GOV (2026-10-13): each function divides between county and city by the state's shares in the Census 2022 Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances by type of government (data/research/budgets/local-spending-by-type.json).
replacement: Census FY2024 individual government finances (data/source/government-finances) for each county and city, with estimates for the rest.

whatItFakes: Each new fiscal year's budget is adopted on its start date by carrying the year's amounts forward.
why: Councils and legislatures can't vote budgets until M3 (owner, Oct 10: old budget rules until councils vote).
replacement: Resolved Oct 20: in a played year in Rollingwood TX, East Sandwich MA and Holdrege NE every government (federal, state, county, city) adopted its 2025 budget by its body's recorded vote; the carry-forward remains only as the fallback when no body votes (pool item gov-stopgap-budgets-missing-engine).

whatItFakes: A mayor's veto is overridden by two thirds of the members voting; ordinances take effect 30 days after enactment.
why: Each city's charter sets its own override majority and effective date; they aren't read yet.
replacement: Override majorities and ordinance effective dates from each state's municipal code and sampled charters, with estimates for the rest.
resolvedBy: OPUS-GOV, Oct 12: two thirds of each body's whole membership (vetoOverrideShare, sourced in FIXER's stand-in figures).

whatItFakes: Committee seats go to each party's most senior members by the chamber's party ratio; real committees are appointed by the presiding officer or a committee on committees. Committee size is now sourced (about 11 members, 5 to 20; Book of the States 2023, Table 3.23).
why: Each body's committee rules, sizes, assignments and chairs aren't read yet.
replacement: Leadership appoints committee members (leadership races and chamber leadership research, #3788's chamber-leadership.json).

whatItFakes: On a statewide ballot measure, the voters the world doesn't name vote as even lean bands around the state's 2024 presidential lean, sized by the state's 2024 vote, each band voting its own view of the question (no separate public-opinion level for the policy).
why: CORE's voter groups aren't populated in generated worlds, and OPUS-PEOPLE's views engine (with issue opinion beyond left-right) isn't built.
replacement: CORE's populated voter groups across the state, each voting from PEOPLE's views of the question.

whatItFakes: A recall petition's signatures from the town's unnamed voters are the named residents' signing share times the town's estimated electorate (population times the 2024 voting share), against whatever signature base the state's rule names.
why: CORE's voter groups and real voter rolls aren't populated in generated worlds.
replacement: Signatures gathered by the organizer's and volunteers' real contacts, plus CORE's voter groups, counted against the rule's own base (registered voters or last vote cast).

whatItFakes: An employers' group's lobbyist is the owner of the member business the bill costs most (when they live in town, are not barred and their traits lean to serve), else the best-paid town resident working for it; the group does not hire one.
why: Owners now decide to join and pay dues (Oct 14), but lobbyists aren't a hired job yet.
replacement: The group hires a lobbyist (a person with a job, a record and memory of each member's votes). Owner as lobbyist done Oct 19.

whatItFakes: A staffer hired where no government treasury is open (no budgets module) holds the post without pay; with budgets open they're on the payroll of the government their official serves.
why: Public payroll from government treasuries isn't wired in core2 yet (requested from OPUS-CORE).
replacement: Resolved Oct 20: a staffer whose office employer sits where no job exists to follow (a territory's state or federal office) takes the town's schedule and payday (scheduleFromPlaceId), so every aide hired where budgets are open is on a treasury payroll. Shown in staff-paid-every-place.test.ts (pool item gov-stopgap-staff-missing-engine).

whatItFakes: A race the town doesn't vote in is counted on the counted residents' engine at a coarser level (a House district's, the state's counties', a legislative district's eligible voters, voting as the town's counted residents would on each place's 2024 lean), but its candidates are each party's typical candidate (the holder stands for their party with the typical campaign) rather than people with records. A state legislative district reads its own 2024 vote (MIT Election Data and Science Lab, 3,182 of 6,831 Census districts matched; src/core2/legislative-district-results.ts); one the source lacks, a nonpartisan one, or a seat one party did not contest is the state's vote over its districts leaning to its holder's party at the typical margin (legislativeSeatMargin, ESTIMATED, checked against the districts that do have a result).
why: Fictional candidates with records for every seat in the country aren't built (PEOPLE's who runs). The legislative-district results half was sourced in gov-legislative-district-results-2024.
replacement: Each race's candidates as fictional people with records and campaigns (core-world-race-lean-candidates).

whatItFakes: A presidential year's national environment is a fixed shift against the party holding the presidency, with no economy or presidential record behind it.
why: WORLD's economy and the president's record don't feed the race yet; the shift is the campaign parameter presidentialIncumbentPartyShift (TUNABLE). Resolved by SIM-ELECTORATE (2026-10-13): every state's presidential vote is counted in its counties' blocks, and the national environment is read from the economy since the opening (WORLD macro) and the candidates' records (src/core2/electorate-blocks.ts); the missing approval is SG-GOV-electorate-approval.
replacement: A national environment read from the economy (WORLD macro) and the president's record, replacing the fixed incumbent-party shift.

whatItFakes: The wider population's purchases are merged per seller, kind and week of the month and paid monthly instead of after each household's own paydays; count workers always work their full schedule and are paid on the employer's cadence (semimonthly approximated as two monthly dates).
why: Two-level population (owner, Oct 11): only the circle is simulated person by person; the merged flows keep every monthly total equal to the full opening.
replacement: Wider-population spending timed from the counts' pay dates and income, with absence and turnover rates by industry checked against BLS JOLTS and CPS.

whatItFakes: A person filled in from the wider population keeps receiving their retirement income through the residents account; their cash share is their opening share of the residents' current cash, and their job's calendar copies the employer's cadence from the fill-in date.
why: Fill-in v2 moves cash, scheduled work and household purchases onto the person's own records; retirement income is tied to per-person award records funded through the outside payer's single obligation.
replacement: Done Oct 12: a filled-in retiree is paid their own award by the same outside payer on the same dates (the pooled retirement flow shrinks by exactly that amount). The cash share is an estimate from opening shares, and the job's calendar follows the employer's cadence, both by design.

whatItFakes: Buyers outside the town are one account per place paying each firm a fixed weekly share of its projected receipts (adjusted with its demand), not individual outside customers, freight orders, Medicaid claims or guests.
why: 11 of 14 closures in the first money year were firms with no customer route at all (owner order M0-money-fix); the share of receipts from outside the town is researched per industry.
replacement: Outside demand from the national and regional economy engines (OPUS-WORLD): exports, government programs and visitors as their own dated buyers.

whatItFakes: Each firm pays cash above twice its industry's median buffer to owners monthly, a fixed tunable share to the town's residents and the rest outside; no firm has recorded owners, retained-earnings policy, taxes or investment.
why: Without payouts, firms kept every dollar of profit and residents ran out of cash within the year (Mill Creek, Oklahoma: firms +$77M, residents $7.7M to $0).
replacement: OPUS-WORLD's business engine: recorded owners (local people or outside), payout and investment decisions from the firm's own conditions, and business taxes.
resolution: Deleted the core stand-in (the monthly payout flow, its handler and its two parameters). Owners draw from their firm through the business engine: a recorded owner chooses a share of the profit the firm kept from their own money and the firm's cash (business.ts, owner-draw), to local owners as counted or full residents and to outside owners through the recorded outside exchanges.

whatItFakes: Counted residents the opening couldn't place in a town firm (the employment target from ACS/CPS less recorded jobs) earn the place's ACS median earnings (the town's median recorded wage where the place's sample is too thin), paid every two weeks from outside, without employers, commutes or industries.
why: The opening's town workplaces cover only part of the county's industry mix (e.g. 34% in Mill Creek, Oklahoma), so most working residents had no income and the residents' account ran dry within months.
replacement: Recorded jobs for every employed resident: town firms in the missing industries (health care, education, government) and commutes to employers in other places (LEHD LODES origin-destination flows), with their own pay.

whatItFakes: A business closed by its owner's choice pays its workers what they've earned (counted workers at once, full workers on their next payday from cash held back), its supplier bills already owed, then settles each open credit line from the cash left (the rest is written off, as in any closure); no assets are sold, so a firm's equipment and property add nothing to what lenders and the owner receive.
why: WORLD's owners needed a way to close a solvent business; a full wind-down (final pay, settling payables, selling assets) is not built yet.
replacement: The closure sells the business's assets (WORLD's business engine records them) before settling lenders and the owner's distribution.

whatItFakes: The part of each household's assigned living cost (CEX basket plus HUD Fair Market Rent) that is not bought from a recorded local seller and is not carried by a bound contract (rent to a landlord, mortgage to the bank, which the housing engine pays) is paid to one outside account on the 1st: no utility or outside store.
why: Rent and non-local spending were never paid, so household cash grew without limit.
replacement: The outside-spending model (category location-quotient leakage) that pays the non-local basket to outside sellers by category. Rent and mortgages are already paid to recorded landlords and the bank by OPUS-WORLD's housing engine (checked Oct 16, Rush Valley, Utah, seed rent1); turn the rest off with collapseToTwoLevels(input, { outsideLivingCosts: false }) once the model exists.

whatItFakes: A named person filled in from a recorded identity (e.g. a state or federal official) gets neutral traits, no family or acquaintances, no cash and a monthly cadence.
why: Traits, kin and past come from the opening's generation world, which a running core doesn't have; GOV needs full officials now (SG-GOV-official-identity-only).
replacement: PEOPLE's trait, kin and past builders seeded from the world seed and the identity (as fill-in of counted residents does), and the official's pay from the public payroll. Done Oct 12 (OPUS-CORE): fillInIdentity gives traits from PEOPLE's openingTemperaments, seeded by the world and the person.

whatItFakes: Counted adults in the town vote as one group per age band: eligible voters are the count times the place's ACS 2020–2024 citizen share of adults blended with the state's CPS 2024 share for the band, turnout is the state's CPS 2024 citizen turnout (national rows where no state row exists, as for the island areas), and every group starts with its county's 2024 presidential two-party margin as its lean (the state's in Alaska, which reports by house district).
why: In a two-level town only about 60 named people vote individually; elections need the counted population to vote from its own records (PLAY's report on GOV's elections). Resolved by the one-electorate change (owner, Oct 14, 2026): the groups are deleted; every counted adult votes from their own record and place in the town's lean order (src/core2/electorate.ts), counted votes are scaled by the place's ACS citizen share (src/core2/electorate-places.ts citizenShareOf), and CPS 2024 turnout is a check in src/core2/electorate.test.ts, not an input.
replacement: Residents' own views (PEOPLE's views engine) set each group's lean, refined by GOV's elections; each counted person's own citizenship once the counts record it.

whatItFakes: Paid family leave collects the same estimated payroll premium from full workers and counted groups but pays no leave. The generic contribution omits jurisdiction-specific employee/employer splits, wage caps and covered-employment exclusions. Nobody claims leave for a birth, adoption or a relative's illness; no received contribution notice or director explanation is modeled.
why: There is no birth-leave or caregiving event a worker can claim leave from, and no benefit payment route from a treasury to a person.
replacement: PEOPLE: a leave-taking choice on a birth or a relative's serious illness (health engine), and CORE: a benefit payment from a government treasury to a person through the journal (e.g. payBenefit(treasuryId, personId, amountMinor, source)); then GOV pays wage replacement from the premium fund.

whatItFakes: Public-sector collective bargaining raises public workers' pay by an estimated union premium phased in over the first contract years (src/core2/law-reach/group-a-bargaining.ts), but no contract is bargained: there is no bargaining table, unit or negotiation, and the premium is one average for every public job.
why: There is no bargaining engine: no union contract, no bargaining unit wage or table.
replacement: GOV: a bargaining engine that negotiates the unit's contract with the public employer and applies it with CORE's rerateJob(jobId, hourlyMinor, source); WORLD: union membership on workers' records.

whatItFakes: A right-to-work law lowers the local union's dues as membership falls (about four points over five years), but no worker's membership or fee is recorded: the dues are one pooled flow from the wider population, and a named worker keeps paying or not paying exactly as before.
why: Union membership and dues are not on workers' records; the local's dues are one standing flow set from the state's membership rate (src/core2/membership-dues.ts). The law's effect is read by the group A union mechanic (src/core2/law-reach/group-a-union.ts), which scales that flow.
replacement: WORLD or CORE: union membership on named jobs and counted groups, dues as a payroll deduction through the journal, which right-to-work then ends for nonmembers.

whatItFakes: Legal cannabis sales move each household's spending (about $170 per resident a year, estimated from 2024 state sales) from outside the town to the town's existing retail businesses, split by their demand. There are no dedicated licensed dispensaries and no license application. A named adult's use is a seeded draw from their id at the national adult prevalence (src/core2/modules/place-prices.ts), not a state series or a stored record.
why: The place-prices engine reads the law monthly (src/core2/modules/place-prices.ts). The use draw is national, not by state; dispensaries are not founded as businesses.
replacement: WORLD: dispensaries founded through the business engine and licensed by the control board; PEOPLE: state prevalence in place of the national share; WORLD: dispensaries founded through the business engine.

whatItFakes: The credit engine reads the catalog cap when quoting new personal loans for full and counted households. The generic 36% ceiling stands in for product, principal, fee and lender-specific statutory rules. Counted income uses contracted wages adjusted by the latest settled wage-flow fraction; individual counted attendance and historical earnings ledgers are absent. Existing fixed-rate contracts are not retroactively repriced.
why: Personal loans share the borrowing comparison and use borrower-keyed payments in both tiers. Lender exemptions, fee-inclusive APR, statutory product scope and counted individual attendance history are missing. A binding native rate change, received explanation and director chain still need evidence.
replacement: Counted earnings history matching full workers, sourced product-specific rate and fee rules, and a named borrower receiving the explanation and discussing the changed offer.

whatItFakes: The construction engine reads multifamily zoning at each monthly starts decision; a completed home reaching a named household and its informed reaction still need played-world proof.
why: A changed starts calculation is not itself a household housed; the full law-to-person chain remains unproven.
replacement: WORLD: a housing engine with lots, units and construction decisions (e.g. addHousingCapacity(placeId, units) driven by builders' returns).

whatItFakes: Housing spending pays rent help to the lowest-cash renting households the extra money covers (a monthly payment from the treasury to the household's head, no more than the rent), but only to full households: counted renting households are not reached.
why: Counted renters have no per-household lease to pay toward; they are pooled flows.
replacement: Counted renting households read by the same rule, times their count, once counted rent flows are keyed per household (world-counted-law-payouts-keyed).

whatItFakes: The inclusionary law now sets construction shares and returns, but the completed-unit allocation handles full leases only.
why: Counted households must use the same affordable-unit allocation, and a paid rent change needs a received notice and director line.
replacement: WORLD: the housing engine's new units, with the set-aside share priced below market for eligible households.

whatItFakes: Rent renewal reads stabilization for full leases and counted rent flows, but applies the catalog's estimated cap to every rented building. A full tenant gets a renewal notice (the law, old rent, market rent, charged rent) and learns of the saving; a counted tenant gets no notice.
why: Building exemptions and enacted cap terms are not yet resolved; a counted tenant is not a person who can be told.
replacement: Resolve the statute's cap and building exemptions from records; counted tenants are told in the same share when they are filled in as a full person.

whatItFakes: Eviction hearings now read the counsel law and pay the funding treasury's outside provider before offering full or counted households a repayment plan; the provider is not a named legal-services organization.
why: Counsel payment and settlement records exist, but a delivered notice, informed tenant reaction and director line are not yet connected.
replacement: Use a legal-services provider record and deliver the settlement notice, then prove the paid case, informed tenant stance and director line in a played world.

whatItFakes: Partnering with immigration enforcement reaches an estimated count of noncitizen adults (national share) instead of named noncitizens.
why: People have no citizenship record.
replacement: PEOPLE: citizenship and immigration status on people and counted residents (ACS B05001 by place); then the policy reaches the named people it covers.
resolution: The enforcement-partnership law reaches named noncitizen adults and counted members by one rule: citizenship is a seeded draw from each person's id against their place's ACS share of adult citizens, blended with the state's (src/core2/citizenship.ts), read the same for full people and counted members (counted-reach.ts, law-reach/group-a-records.ts).

whatItFakes: Ending cash bail records the right on adults and an estimated count of people held before trial. The justice engine now reads the law for charged officials awaiting a bribery trial (held when they cannot post the estimated $10,000 bail), but no one else is arrested or held and bail is one flat estimate.
why: The justice engine hears only corruption cases; there is no arrest engine for other crimes. Oct 19: pretrial detention for charged defendants is built (src/core2/justice-pretrial.ts).
replacement: GOV: a justice engine with arrests, charges, pretrial detention and release decisions from the law in force.
resolution: The public-safety engine arrests people from the town's crime measures and decides each defendant's wait for trial from the bail law and their cash (src/core2/public-safety.ts); jail days are paid by the county treasury.

whatItFakes: Felony disenfranchisement takes each state's share of the voting-eligible population (The Sentencing Project, Locked Out 2024; the national share for D.C. and the territories the report omits) and half of it back where a restoration law is in force, instead of people's own records.
why: People have no conviction or sentence records.
replacement: GOV and PEOPLE: conviction and sentence records on people and counted residents; voting eligibility then reads each record.

whatItFakes: Child access prevention records the storage duty on every adult in a household with a child, not only gun owners.
why: Gun ownership isn't recorded. Resolved Oct 16: each household keeps a firearm or not by its own draw against its state's survey rate (RAND 2020, `firearm-ownership.ts`), counted households by the same rate as a group, and the storage duty reaches only adults in owning households with a child.
replacement: PEOPLE: firearm ownership on households (from survey rates by state, seeded per household at generation).

whatItFakes: Independent redistricting records the rule on legislators, but no district lines are drawn by anyone.
why: There is no redistricting engine, and no districting event happens in a played year: state and House districts are fixed Census joins (src/districts), the starting lines are the 2026 plans, and the next apportionment is after the 2030 census. Checked Oct 15 (Claude, pool laws-family-government-operations): no code in src/core2 draws a district or reads this law. The design exists (docs/codex/specs/bank/b16-redistricting-vra.md; owner D-6 and Sept 28 #8); the work is pool item gov-redistricting-engine.
replacement: GOV: a redistricting step after each census that draws districts, run by the commission when this law is in force.

whatItFakes: For an island area the budgets module records no residents, group B shares a budget line's change to the town by the Census population in its own parameter table.
why: data/research/money/public-budget-bases.json has no population2024 (and no budget) for Puerto Rico, Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa or the Northern Mariana Islands. Resolved Oct 19: public-budget-bases.json already carries each island area's population (islandAreaPopulation2020 and puertoRicoPopulation2025), and the budgets module now reads it into the state government's residents.
replacement: OPUS-GOV budgets: public-budget-bases.json carries each island area's population and finances (Census Island Areas, PR government finances); group B then reads GovernmentRow.residents only.

whatItFakes: Where the town has no public school employer, teachers and staff at the town's private school stand in for public school staff: a teacher-salary floor and a schools budget line reach them.
why: The core opening never imports the town's public schools as an employer (no service:school jobs in generated worlds), so a public-school pay law has no one to reach.
replacement: OPUS-CORE imports the town's public school district as a service:school employer with its staff (NCES district and CCD staff counts); the stand-in is dropped and only public school jobs are covered. Done Oct 15: the district import (opening-public-schools.ts) had already landed; the private-school stand-in in law-reach/group-b.ts and its data row are deleted, so the salary floor and the schools line reach only public school staff.

whatItFakes: The price engine now reads fare-free transit and refunds each full and counted household's estimated fare expenditure.
why: Trips remain consumption estimates, and a received notice must connect the saving to an informed view and director line.
replacement: Replace remaining estimated-use or provider assumptions with their records and prove the journal payment, received notice, informed stance and director line in a played world.

whatItFakes: The price engine now reads the mileage law at payment and offsets estimated fuel tax for each household; miles and fuel use are consumption estimates.
why: Vehicle use is not yet metered on household records, and the paid adjustment lacks a received explanation and director line.
replacement: Replace remaining estimated-use or provider assumptions with their records and prove the journal payment, received notice, informed stance and director line in a played world.

whatItFakes: The price engine now pays the law's treasury for cheaper broadband and offsets the estimated old bill for full and counted households.
why: A public provider, individual subscription choice and actual old service contract still need records; a subscription share remains registered in SG-WORLD-prices-household-shares.
replacement: Replace remaining estimated-use or provider assumptions with their records and prove the journal payment, received notice, informed stance and director line in a played world.

whatItFakes: Medicaid expansion pays each covered adult the average medical spending (BLS CEX drugs plus medical supplies), the federal treasury paying the Medicaid match in force and the state treasury the rest, and its work requirement stops that for the adults it reaches; there are no itemized medical bills or health plans for the payment to settle.
why: The core has no itemized medical bills or health plans for people; the payment is the average spending, not a bill.
replacement: OPUS-PEOPLE health engine: setCoverage(personId, { plan: "medicaid", from, to }) and counted-group coverage shares, read by medical costs (OPUS-CORE household spending).

whatItFakes: The baseline SNAP benefit is the maximum allotment less 30 percent of net income, from wages, retirement benefits and household size alone. Shelter, child-care and medical deductions, the asset test, categorical eligibility, the elderly and disabled rules, immigrant rules and the work-program participation the law also reaches are not modeled.
why: The federal treasury owes each qualifying household one monthly payment (law-reach group B, group-b-food-aid.ts), read by the household's cash and spending. The core records a household's wages and retirement awards, not its rent, child care or medical bills, so those deductions have nothing to read.
replacement: Per-household shelter, dependent-care and medical expense records read by the benefit (world housing and health costs), and the other income programs (SSI, TANF) a household receives.

whatItFakes: Universal preschool pays the household of each 3- and 4-year-old the state's spending per enrolled child (NIEER) times an estimated enrolled share; no child is recorded as enrolled and no child-care bill changes.
why: There is no school enrollment or child-care spending in the core.
replacement: OPUS-PEOPLE schools engine: enroll(childId, schoolOrgId, { program: "pre-k" }) and OPUS-CORE household child-care cost, reduced when enrolled.

whatItFakes: A voucher pays the state's share of the average private tuition each household is already charged (opening-private-tuition, spread over the town's families), not the tuition of the children who actually attend a private school.
why: No child is enrolled at a school, so a payment can't follow a student; the tuition a household pays is the town's NCES average spread over its families.
replacement: OPUS-PEOPLE schools engine: enrollment(childId) naming the school; then the voucher follows the enrolled child to the school each term.

whatItFakes: The existing assessment and tax bill now read the cap law and settle full and counted owners through their own accounts. A yes/no catalog law still uses a generic estimated assessment cap rather than statutory levy-versus-assessment scope, exemptions or ownership-reset terms.
why: Session A wires the existing property-tax engine. The catalog has no numeric statutory cap or exemption terms, and the world has no delivered tax notice linking the assessment to an informed stance and director line.
replacement: Record each cap statute's size, scope, exemptions and ownership-reset terms; apply them at assessment and prove the bill, received notice, informed stance and director line for a named owner.

whatItFakes: Sales tax rates and a grocery exemption are price records on household heads and retailers; purchases collect no sales tax for any treasury.
why: Household purchase flows (finance contracts, the residents purchase flows) have no tax line.
replacement: OPUS-CORE purchase API: setPurchaseTax({ placeId, category: "all"|"groceries", ratePercent, payeeAccountId }) applied to each household purchase and remitted to the treasury.
resolvedBy: OPUS-GOV, Oct 12: budgets sets each level's sales tax in force on every purchase in town through the core's setPurchaseTax (v21), each level's share to its treasury, groceries exempt where an exemption is law; re-set when a sales-tax law takes effect.

whatItFakes: A gas-hookup ban raises the housing engine's new-construction cost (modules/housing.ts sets allElectric, housing-construction.ts prices it into single and multifamily starts), but no household's appliance fuel choice or utility bill changes.
why: Construction cost by code is read; fuel choice and household energy bills aren't modeled, so the ban's effect on a household stops at the price and supply of new homes.
replacement: A household energy-bill and appliance-fuel record read by the ban once utilities are modeled.

whatItFakes: The price engine now charges clean-electricity and carbon costs to full and counted households under the law in force; metered use remains estimated.
why: The payment reaches the journal, but no delivered bill yet connects the recipient's informed stance and director line.
replacement: Replace remaining estimated-use or provider assumptions with their records and prove the journal payment, received notice, informed stance and director line in a played world.

whatItFakes: The price engine charges container deposits to full and counted households under the live law. Container use and redemption still use household estimates rather than each person's purchases and return decision.
why: Per-container charges now settle on the journal, but return transactions and a received bill-to-view/director chain are missing.
replacement: Recorded container purchases and return transactions, plus a delivered explanation that an affected person can cite.

whatItFakes: A clean air plan binds the town's industrial employers (compliance record) wherever it's law, whether or not the county is in nonattainment.
why: No EPA Green Book nonattainment list is loaded for counties.
replacement: Load EPA Green Book nonattainment counties as data; the plan then binds emitters only in listed counties, and OPUS-WORLD business costs read the compliance record. Done Oct 15 (Claude, pool laws-family-clean-air): the EPA Green Book county list is loaded (data/business/nonattainment.json) and the business engine charges only emitters in listed counties, citing the clean air plan law row where one is in force (routeCompliance, business.ts); the generic employer rows are gone.

whatItFakes: Groundwater law now reaches the existing agricultural output limit and outside-sales flows. The generic withdrawal share and irrigation elasticity stand in for actual farm pumping, irrigated acreage and crop response. Natural-resource budget services and non-farm water exposure remain unwired.
why: No farm irrigation exposure or pumping record exists. No mine or utility water-use record justifies extending the agricultural elasticity to them. The one-input operating-rule slot cannot combine independent restrictions; an existing unrelated restriction is preserved. A received explanation and complete owner/director chain remain unproved.
replacement: Read farm water use and crop exposure, statutory allocations and independent restrictions at production; wire non-farm use and resource services only from their own records, then prove sales, owner choice, received knowledge and director line.

whatItFakes: Farmland protection reduces new-housing starts through the housing engine (zoning farmlandProtected, housing-construction.ts), but there are no land parcels, so which fields stay farmland and what farms earn don't change.
why: Development is read as a share of buildable land; individual parcels and farm use aren't modeled.
replacement: Land parcels with a use and an owner, read by new construction and by farm output.

whatItFakes: Where the town's records hold no government building, its polling places have no building and a kind of "unread"; where they hold one, every precinct votes in it.
why: Polling place facility types (schools, churches, community centers, government buildings) by state are not read yet; the EAVS national brief reports the count of voting locations, not their kinds.
replacement: Each state's polling place facility types from the EAC's full EAVS dataset and the town's own buildings of those kinds (its schools, churches and halls) as recorded places, one per precinct.

whatItFakes: The highways line is a road service level record on drivers and road builders; commute time and vehicle costs don't change.
why: There is no road condition or commuting cost in the core.
replacement: OPUS-WORLD regional engine: setRoadCondition({ placeId, level }) read by commute time and vehicle costs.

whatItFakes: The higher education line is a support level record on 18-to-24-year-olds; no tuition is charged or changed.
why: No college enrollment or tuition exists in the core.
replacement: OPUS-PEOPLE schools engine: college enrollment and tuition (setTuition({ institutionId, inStateMinor })) read by household spending.

whatItFakes: The parks line is a service level record on residents and recreation firms; no one's time use or well-being changes.
why: People's leisure doesn't read park service levels.
replacement: OPUS-PEOPLE time-use and needs: park service level read by leisure choices and well-being (placeService({ placeId, service: "parks", level })).

whatItFakes: A territory's delegate race the town doesn't vote in is decided at its 2024 delegate race's lean with no voters counted: the race row shows no votes.
why: The Clerk's House tables the game reads hold no delegate districts outside D.C., and the territories' eligible voters are not in the data (CPS does not survey them).
replacement: Each territory's 2024 delegate race votes cast (its election office's certified results) sizing the place, so it is counted on the election engine like any district.

whatItFakes: Election-day weather adds nothing to any voter's cost of voting: every election day is fair weather.
why: The played world keeps no weather record; the storm catalog (data/source/storm-events-2000-2024) lists past episodes, but no engine writes a storm on a game day yet. Retired by Session C, October 15, 2026: the helper returned zero without reading any weather record. The weather reason and its numeric term were removed from all turnout tiers; the game no longer presents a weather reading.
replacement: Retired the unsupported weather reason. A future weather effect requires an actual place-and-day weather record, with the same reader for named, counted, and wider voters.

whatItFakes: Where the state's law settles an exact election tie by lot (about 34 states for general elections, 51 for primaries), the game holds a second election between the tied candidates instead.
why: A lot is a random draw, and the owner's no-dice rule bars a seeded draw from deciding an outcome; the owner hasn't ruled on legally required lots.
replacement: RESOLVED (owner, Oct 14, 2026: ties follow the law of the state, a recorded lot where the law says lot): src/core2/election-ties.ts draws the lot from a stable hash of the contest and the tied candidates and keeps it as a tie record (citation, tied candidates, each slip, the result).

whatItFakes: A town's filing deadline where the state's municipal rule is unread (its row in filing-deadlines.json is 'unread'): the median number of days between the candidate filing deadline and the primary over the places with a 2026 row (85 days before the election). Rows tagged ESTIMATED there were read from search excerpts or summaries, not the current code.
why: Many states write the deadline against a primary, a charter or a window the town calendar does not hold, and each statute must be read to structure it.
replacement: Each unread state's deadline rule read from its code into src/core2/data/elections/filing-deadlines.json, and each ESTIMATED row checked against the current statute.

whatItFakes: Where a place's filing row carries no filing office, minimum age or voter-registration rule (county offices in Alaska, Connecticut, Rhode Island, D.C. and the territories; municipal offices in Hawaii and two territories; Vermont's legislature), the median of the read values for that office family and the generic clerk title stand in.
why: The place's law was not read into filing-requirements.json.
replacement: Each place's own rule read into data/research/elections/filing-requirements.json.

whatItFakes: The date of a special election where the state's law leaves the day to the governor: 90 days after the vacancy (parameters.json). special-election-law.json reads the law for every state and territory whose legislative vacancies are filled by election (U.S. House rows for 51 places, legislative rows for the rest) and records 33 rows as governor-sets-date; the days-after-vacancy rows are ESTIMATED nominal values inside each statutory window.
why: Each state's timing statute (days after the vacancy, the governor's call, the next general election) per office family has to be read.
replacement: A row per state and office family in src/core2/data/elections/special-election-law.json read from the state's code.

whatItFakes: For 6 of the 56 places (American Samoa, the Northern Mariana Islands, the Virgin Islands, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin and Indiana) the ballot-order rule is read from a secondary source or partly from search snippets of the law, not its text; the other 14 places the Oct 19 research read are set from the statute.
why: Ballotpedia's ballot-order page gives one rule per state, usually for the general election; NCSL's table and the state codes were not reachable from the research session.
replacement: Each estimated row checked against its statute (the state election code, or the territory's) and its estimate flag cleared.

whatItFakes: Every printed ballot lists its candidates in the order they filed, so the first to file takes the first-listed edge in every precinct.
why: Each state's ballot-order law (alphabetical, rotation by precinct, a drawing, the incumbent's or the governor's party first) is not read into data yet.
replacement: RESOLVED (CTO, Oct 14, 2026: closed by the law of the place): src/core2/ballot-order.ts reads each of the 56 places' ballot-order rule from data/research/elections/ballot-order-2026.json (alphabetical, a drawn alphabet, a lot per contest, rotation by precinct, by party, the incumbent first), and every voter reads the form of the ballot they hold.

whatItFakes: Everyone in the line of succession to the presidency is taken to be a natural-born citizen and 14 years a resident; only the age of 35 is checked.
why: People's records hold no place of birth by citizenship or years of residence in the United States. Resolved Oct 15 (core-stopgap-succession-missing-record): an official's birth is a past fact (identity:nativity), drawn from the world's seed against the state's native-born share of adults (ACS 2020-2024, table B05003); the president and vice president are native by the law; the line passes over anyone whose record is foreign-born or shows under 14 years of residence.
replacement: OPUS-PEOPLE: citizenship at birth and years of residence on a person's record; the line then passes over anyone who fails U.S. Const. art. II, sec. 1, cl. 5.

whatItFakes: Where a state's tie rule depends on race size (a new election for a large race, a lot for a small one) and its data row names no statute number, the line between them: 1,000 votes cast. North Carolina's row reads its statute's 5,000 (G.S. 163-182.8); no other state's row has a size rule yet.
why: The tie-rules research names some size rules without the number; the CTO ruled for the owner (Oct 14, 2026) that the statute's number is used where the data names one, else this ESTIMATED row.
replacement: The statute's size line in data/research/elections/tie-rules-2026.json. Built Oct 16: a small-race rule must carry the statute's own line (atOrBelowVotes); the 1,000-vote estimate and its parameter are deleted.

whatItFakes: A member of a deciding body who is a named official the world has not filled in as a person has no recorded views, so their party's side stands in for their lean when they vote on a tie.
why: Named officials without a person record have no traits or views.
replacement: OPUS-PEOPLE: a filled-in person for each official the moment they decide something, with their own views. Done Oct 15 (claude/elections-tie-named-member-lean): a member the world has not seated as a person is filled in by holderOf the moment they decide, and votes from their recorded views (officialLean); a member with no record at all abstains.

whatItFakes: A named person is never barred from voting for a felony conviction; the state's share is taken off the counted electorate instead.
why: The core holds no conviction or sentence records on people. Resolved Oct 16 (laws-stopgap-group-a-voting-missing-record): barredFromVoting reads the person's convictions and sentence on the justice record against the state's restore-voting law in force; counted adults keep the state's share of the same rule.
replacement: GOV and PEOPLE: conviction and sentence records; barredFromVoting then reads the person's own record against the state's law. Done Oct 15: barredFromVoting reads the justice engine's custody record against the place's law (data/research/justice/prison-voting-2026.json); the voter rolls, the primary count, turnout and the director's polling place all read it.

whatItFakes: A local outlet's record name is its kind (newspaper, television, radio); outlets are sized from state counts, not named real outlets.
why: Outlet names are player text and come from the English engine; the per-place outlet roster isn't researched. Resolved by the press (OPUS-PEOPLE, 2026-10-14): each outlet is named at the opening from the world's seed, the place's name and src/core2/data/press/mastheads.json (masthead words, call-sign letters by state); outlets stay sized from state counts.
replacement: Names from the English engine (OPUS-PEOPLE) and per-county outlet rosters from Medill and FCC data.

whatItFakes: P15 kin and temperament generation coefficients (relative proximity, birth spacing, first-birth spread, paternal age gap, men's fertility lag, upbringing shift, facet correlations, reference age) are prototype values.
why: Families and temperaments must be generated now; no instrument-matched source fixes these coefficients yet.
replacement: Coefficients sourced from NSFG, natality and NEO-PI-R facet tables and checked against the P15 answer keys.

whatItFakes: Kin outside the household are generated per resident household as husk-tier people: every relative alive or not by the SSA cohort life table for their birth year (Actuarial Study No. 120, birth decades 1900-2010 interpolated), siblings by size-biased cohort fertility, children and grandchildren by Census children ever born; relatives are never matched to other residents, partners of siblings and adult children and cousins are absent, and residence is only county or state, set by whether each adult moved away (state ACS leaving rates times a tunable share) and whether the parents' marriage held (NSFG).
why: Every resident needs real family consistent with age; a full kin-matching and migration engine does not exist.
replacement: A kin engine that matches relatives to residents across households and places, with partners, cousins and observed migration distances.

whatItFakes: The five temperament dimensions are read from five NEO facets (CTO-approved October 10, 2026) with BLSA age curves, IPIP-NEO sex differences and NEO-PI-R manual facet correlations; the A4 compliance age curve's quadratic term is held at zero because it is not legible in the source manuscript, and each dimension uses one facet rather than its own norms.
why: The owner's five dimensions have no published norms of their own; facet norms are the nearest sourced spread.
replacement: The A4 quadratic term from a legible copy of Terracciano and others (2005) Table 2, and norms measured on the five dimensions themselves.

whatItFakes: Closeness is hours together over hours plus a sourced half-closeness point, fading by a tunable half-life; opening closeness uses the average GSS visit rate for the tie and a registered conversion of answer categories to visits, not each pair's history.
why: No survey measures closeness in hours or its decay without contact; Hall (2019) gives hour thresholds and Roberts and Dunbar (2015) only the direction of decay.
replacement: Closeness calibrated against a panel of measured tie strength and contact (for example, the Roberts and Dunbar network data or a US panel), with per-pair opening histories from the shared past.

whatItFakes: Opening household members are aged from the place's records by household type: the chance of having a partner now comes from a yearly chain of first marriage (ACS 2024 never-married shares by age), divorce (NSFG women's first-marriage survival, used for every marriage), widowhood (SSA 2023 life table, with the spouse's age from the CPS 2023 spouse age gap) and remarriage (NCFMR 2022); a partner's age follows the national CPS 2023 spouse age gap for every couple, including same-sex couples; parents of children under 18 follow national CPS 2023 parents by age and living arrangement; a household of related housemates is always one parent and one grown child; parents' grown children at home are a seeded count from the parent's births and the place's share of adults living in a parent's home (ACS B09021); homes of unrelated housemates take the place's nonfamily household sizes (B11016), each housemate's sex and age drawn on their own. Cohabitation is not a separate path, places outside the ACS 1-year survey read their state, and four territories read the nation (ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE).
why: No source gives each opening adult's partnership history or household; the chain and the CPS tables turn sourced rates into ages by sex and household type. Partnered adults keep the household generator's sex; people living alone and housemates draw sex with age.
replacement: Place-level ACS 5-year sex-by-age, marital-status and household-relationship tables for every seated place and territory, cohabitation and second-marriage survival from NSFG, the spouse age gap and parents' ages by place, and siblings, grandparents raising grandchildren and older parents living in a grown child's home seated as their own household types.

whatItFakes: How far a relative lives changes how often they are visited only by whether they are in the household's county (full pull) or elsewhere in the state (0.39 of it, from Pew 2005 daily contact by same or different town).
why: Relatives outside the town carry only a county or state, not a place, so no travel distance exists to read.
replacement: Travel time between the two people's places once relatives carry a place, from Census Gazetteer place centroids, with visits falling with travel time as measured in a contact-by-distance study.

whatItFakes: Each child's school is a seeded pick among the public schools teaching their entry grade in their place, else in their county and its places, else (for places the county geography does not cover: the territories and Puerto Rico) in their state or territory, weighted by students per grade and shared by children who live together. Attendance boundaries, chosen public schools (19% of students in NCES 2016), private schools and homeschooling are not modeled; the 2023-24 directory stands in for earlier decades; the 815 schools without a reported grade span (all 28 in American Samoa) are left out, so American Samoa keeps generated school names.
why: No attendance boundary or historical school directory is in the repository; P12 supplies each public school's place, grades and enrollment.
replacement: NCES EDGE school attendance boundaries (SABS) with the household's location, private school (PSS) and homeschool shares by state, and historical CCD directories for each cohort's years.

whatItFakes: Residents of the same opening employer are split into seeded balanced workgroups of at most openingCoworkerGroupSize, and each pair knows the other by name since the later of their two start dates. Departments, shifts, earlier jobs and coworkers outside the town are not modeled, and coworkers gain no closeness from working together.
why: Employers carry no departments or teams, and no source gives how many coworkers a person knows.
replacement: Workgroups from occupation and establishment records (BLS OEWS staffing patterns by industry) and a measured number of coworkers known, with time worked together adding to closeness on the shifts both attend.

whatItFakes: Grief starts at the closeness to the person who died and halves every personal half-life; the half-life spread is solved from two Bonanno et al. (2002) pattern shares with 'little grief' set at a quarter of the starting grief (TUNABLE). Grief pulls toward rest and contact with family and holds back organizing with tunable weights. Losses are kept in memory, not in a save.
why: Owner's ruling, October 10, 2026 (CTO on #3942): a personal resilience line, calibrated to about 46% with little grief by 6 months and 15.6% still grieving at 18 months; P10 reported a widow organizing on the day her husband died.
replacement: A grief measure matched to a bereavement instrument (for example the grief items Bonanno et al. used), choice weights checked against observed behavior after a loss, and losses saved with the world.

whatItFakes: Falling-outs in the shared past build from the years a pair shared a class or workgroup and both people's conflict and reliability traits, with tunable trait weights; the base rate is solved to YouGov's lifetime share of adults who ended a friendship, which counts all friendships, not only classmates and coworkers. Favors are not generated: no dated recorded need (a move, a job loss, an illness) exists in the shared past.
why: CTO, October 10, 2026 (#3938): generate favors and falling-outs in the shared past so the director can bring a person back with stakes. Resolved Oct 16, 2026 (core-standins-opening-deletions): deleted. Nothing read the falling-out facts (no engine or director line used them), so they were a record with no read; the two-level rule gives nobody a full past before they are filled in. The generator, its data and its three parameters are gone.
replacement: A friendship-ending rate among classmates and coworkers by years known, temperament weights checked against a study of conflict and personality, and favors from dated recorded needs.

whatItFakes: A person's free hours are filled from one scoring pass per activation: at most one act per need each day, and every act after the activation's own pick must score above zero. Between planned days, needs other than company are held at their activation value and lowered only by the planned acts' own effects; the plan lives in memory, not in a save, and the ATUS caregiving time per participant-day stands for one act of care.
why: The CTO's part 2b decision (October 10, 2026): one scoring pass per free block for daily-tier people and a week planned forward for weekly-tier people, within 20% of part 2's speed.
replacement: A complete daily time budget that reserves the ATUS time of activities the game does not model, needs that evolve on each planned day from their own causes, and plans saved with the world.

whatItFakes: Favors in the shared past come only at a resident's recorded move into the county, from people they shared a class or workgroup with, by closeness at the time from a tunable hours-per-shared-year; the rate is solved to an opt-in commercial poll (39% first ask friends for help moving). Residents' birthplaces are all their own town, so an adult move reads as moving back; job losses and illness come in part 5's lived years.
why: CTO, October 10, 2026, 8:12 p.m. (#3938): generate dated moves first, then favors from close classmates or coworkers at the time of a move. Resolved Oct 16, 2026 (core-standins-opening-deletions): deleted with the falling-outs. No engine read a favor fact; recorded moves keep their own facts, and a favor between two people would come from a dated need in play, not a generated past.
replacement: A probability-sample source on help received at a move, closeness at the time from a measured friendship model, out-of-town birthplaces from ACS place of birth, and favors at job losses and illness.

whatItFakes: New people are met only on a visit (the host's household) and on joining a group (its other members); the first tie holds the act's hours. Meetings at an organized meeting wait for attendance, and new coworkers for jobs changing during play (M1).
why: Owner's ruling, October 10, 2026 (CTO on #3956): build encounters 1 and 2 now, 3 with M1's jobs work.
replacement: Encounters at meetings with attendance, new coworkers when jobs change, neighbors once addresses exist, and first-tie hours checked against a study of how acquaintances form.

whatItFakes: Relatives living outside the town (husk-tier kin) keep only their family and move facts at the opening; their own schooling, work and era history is not generated.
why: They never act, and generating that history for every relative made the prepared town too large to serialize (La Homa: 861 MB of past facts with part 1).
replacement: Generate a relative's deep past when the game first simulates them (promotion from husk tier), from the same deep-past rules residents use.

whatItFakes: Opening views read the person's state and age band (the CES cell), their education and faith profile (opening-profile.ts, itself a stopgap) and a household heritage; the 14 values and issue stances at the opening are not formed. Stances move only on events with a topic and on speeches.
why: First version of views on the new core, built while the people records gain education and faith.
replacement: Opening views from the person's education, faith, place type and upbringing through CES-derived weights; the 14 values; conversations and news moving stances (M1-10, M2-09).

whatItFakes: Old smooth family-plan coefficients; living-cost and household-size housing proxies, recorded affect health proxy, identity gender carrier proxy, successful planned singleton pregnancy with fixed conception-relative duration, infant inactive discretionary tier until future development work.
why: Part 1 precedes housing/jobs integrations; clinical reproductive capacity, infertility and pregnancy outcomes are not represented by the current people records. Rates cannot select pregnancies.
replacement: Source-matched individual reproductive/clinical records, dated pregnancy outcomes, dwelling capacity and coupled choice calibration; infant development producer. Finisher must review these limits against Part 1.

whatItFakes: Opening still-pregnant plans use current opening money, housing, health and temperament as pre-opening proxies, with real recorded partnership and child dates. Reviews occur at 91-day phases anchored to partnership or youngest child; both partners must agree through the chooser. No surveyed fertility rate decides pregnancy.
why: No prenatal records exist in P15 opening population; starting with none depresses the entire first year and synchronizes deliveries.
replacement: OPUS-PEOPLE dated lived pregnancy/resource/medical history, or a finisher/CTO accepted reconstruction with validated first-year calibration.

whatItFakes: How much each recorded reason weighs in deciding to run for office, and the pull of staying out.
why: The research names the reasons (interest, a personal stake, temperament, money, time, age) but not their sizes in this model.
replacement: Weights checked against candidate counts per seat across drawn places once GOV's contests run every cycle (M2-04).

whatItFakes: P10 drive, perception, response and event-severity coefficients are prototype starting values without measured bounds.
why: A starting value is required for drives to form and fade; no instrument-matched source fixes these coefficients yet.
replacement: Coefficients checked against P9 life replays and real bereaved/harmed-cohort spreads of civic action.

whatItFakes: Drive formation as one scored choice among response rows (carry on, take up a cause, hold a grudge, guard family, prove oneself, answer a calling), using the shared chooser and trait-act table; the response set and goal pressures are prototype assumptions.
why: Event-born drives were zero in P8 (acceptance d); the decision path is real but its response set and weights are uncalibrated.
replacement: Response rows and pressures calibrated against documented responses to bereavement, job loss and injustice (P9 lives, panel studies).

whatItFakes: Trait-weighted perception channels (loss, others' distress, injustice, threat, persuasion) choosing which traits raise or lower an event's weight; channel membership is authored.
why: The owner approved bounded perception; no source maps these traits to event salience yet.
replacement: Channel rows and weights validated against appraisal research and P9 replays.
